java/07.text: Inheritance states an is-a relationship: a subclass must honor every promise callers rely on. Composition states a has-a relationship: the object delegates to a collaborator. Overriding changes behavior behind the same method contract; overloading chooses from different parameter signatures at compile time. Prefer composition when you only need reuse. An abstract class can share protected implementation, while an interface exposes a contract without forcing one parent hierarchy.

java/08.text: A sealed type declares a finite family of permitted implementations. It fits a known set such as success and not-found. An open interface fits third-party adapters better. Default methods add behavior to interfaces but must not create conflicting hidden state. A service depends on the interface; infrastructure implements that port instead of controlling the domain.

java/10.text: Generics put element contracts in the compiler. List<String> prevents adding an Integer, but erasure means most type arguments are not reified at runtime. A ? extends T collection produces T; a ? super T collection consumes T. Hash lookup is expected constant time under suitable hashing; sorting normally costs O(n log n). These estimates do not excuse an unbounded web response.

java/13.text: A LocalDate describes a day; Instant describes a timestamp. ZonedDateTime adds timezone rules. Never infer a store timezone from the server location. String.length counts UTF-16 code units; supplementary characters may use two. Use UTF-8 for portable files and select Locale explicitly for language-dependent case conversion.

java/16.text: ExecutorService owns an execution policy; callers own deadlines and cancellation. A Future.get timeout stops waiting, not necessarily the operation. Preserve interruption intent rather than swallowing InterruptedException. Virtual threads are newer than this Java 17 baseline; they reduce waiting-thread costs without removing database or CPU limits. In production, configure a bounded queue instead of the convenience unbounded queue used in this two-task demonstration.

python-first-api/06.text: Use a tuple for a fixed positional group, a list for order, a set for uniqueness, and a dict for key lookup. Comprehensions construct values; generators produce them lazily. Repeated dictionary lookup helps an in-memory catalog. A million database rows should be filtered by a query rather than loaded into Python.
python-first-api/06.code:
notes = [{"id": 1, "title": "APIs"}, {"id": 2, "title": "Python"}]
by_id = {note["id"]: note for note in notes}
titles = sorted(note["title"] for note in notes)
assert by_id[1]["title"] == "APIs"
print(titles)

python-first-api/07.text: An import evaluates a module and reuses its module object. Keep side effects out of imports so tests can load functions without starting servers. A package has a public surface; helpers remain implementation details. A virtual environment isolates dependencies, not untrusted code. Lock dependencies and review installation hooks.
python-first-api/07.code:
from pathlib import Path
from importlib.util import find_spec

print(Path("notes.json").suffix)
assert find_spec("json") is not None

python-first-api/08.text: Use try/except for expected exceptions, else for success-only work, and finally for unconditional cleanup. A context manager packages setup and cleanup into with. Exception chaining preserves the cause for server diagnostics; safe API errors must not serialize that chain. Catch specific failures instead of masking programming bugs as empty catalogs.

python-first-api/09.text: A dataclass generates data-object methods. A Protocol describes structural behavior for adapters without requiring one inheritance hierarchy. An annotation aids static analysis; Pydantic or explicit checks validate runtime input. A union describes alternatives; omitted input is different from a required field whose value may be None.

python-first-api/17.text: A repository owns SQL and connection lifetime. Placeholders bind values, not SQL identifiers; choose identifiers from an allowlist. SQLite is useful for local teaching, with transactions and constraints. An in-memory database lives only as long as its connection, so connection ownership affects test correctness.
python-first-api/17.code:
import sqlite3

with sqlite3.connect(":memory:") as db:
    db.execute("CREATE TABLE notes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL)")
    db.execute("INSERT INTO notes(title) VALUES (?)", ("APIs",))
    title = db.execute("SELECT title FROM notes WHERE id = ?", (1,)).fetchone()[0]
    assert title == "APIs"
    print(title)

nodejs/07.text: The call stack finishes synchronous work before promise continuations run. Timers specify earliest eligibility, not exact execution time. Excessive microtasks can starve other work. Measure event-loop delay under load. A long synchronous transform still blocks other requests inside an async function.

nodejs/09.text: AbortController communicates cancellation intent. The called API must support the signal; abort does not undo a committed write. Clear timers and close resources in finally. Use one request deadline across layers rather than a fresh unrestricted timeout for every call.

nodejs/17.text: Readable, writable, and transform streams move chunks, not whole files. When a writable cannot keep up, producers must wait for drain; pipeline coordinates backpressure and propagates failures. Validate byte ranges before opening a bounded stream; return 206 or 416 deliberately. Destroy streams on client disconnect.

spring-boot/04.text: SpringApplication creates the application context, selects configuration, discovers components, and starts the embedded server. Auto-configuration is conditional on the classpath, environment, and existing beans. Inspect the conditions report when behavior surprises you. Constructor injection declares required dependencies; starting workers in a constructor hides lifecycle ownership.

spring-boot/05.text: A bean is managed by the Spring context. Singleton means one instance per context, not per world-wide deployment. Component scanning starts at declared packages. Lifecycle callbacks define initialization and cleanup. Proxies implement concerns such as transactions; calling through this can bypass interception. Prototype beans need explicit cleanup ownership.

spring-boot/13.text: @Transactional normally applies through a proxy. Keep transactions around related database changes rather than slow external calls. Optimistic locking detects a stale version. An outbox row commits with a business row and publishes later. A retry after an unknown response must keep the original idempotency key.

spring-boot/17.text: MVC commonly uses blocking handlers and JDBC. WebFlux uses reactive streams and can avoid blocked request threads when important I/O boundaries use compatible nonblocking drivers. A blocking driver on an event-loop path loses that benefit. Reactive code adds debugging and context costs; choose it for measured concurrency needs.
spring-boot/17.code:
Blocking: request -> MVC thread -> JDBC wait -> response
Reactive: request -> event loop -> nonblocking driver -> continuation -> response
CPU work: both need a bounded worker boundary

system-design/02.text: Assume 1,200 active readers, one read per minute, and a peak multiplier of five. Average reads are 1200 / 60 = 20 RPS; assumed peak is 100 RPS. At 10 KiB per response, this is roughly 1 MiB/s before overhead. These are planning assumptions, not measured throughput. Measure tail latency and errors before promising capacity.

system-design/14.text: RPO is the tolerable lost-data interval; RTO is the tolerable recovery time. Daily backups have a potential one-day RPO unless log recovery improves it. Offsite copies protect against site loss, but a restore drill proves usability. Record restore duration, checksums, row counts, safe credential handling, and the recovery owner.

mcp/04.text: Pin the wire revision. The supplied course targets 2026-07-28 self-contained requests with per-request capabilities. The 2025-11-25 initialization handshake is a different path; do not combine the models by guesswork. Unsupported features need a supported fallback or a safe rejection. Optional extensions require explicit support checks.

mcp/09.text: Elicitation lets the host ask a user for input. Accept, decline, and cancel need defined continuations. Never collect secrets through a generic form when secure authorization is needed. Roots express filesystem intent, not path confinement. Sampling stays under host policy; support is revision-specific.
